mechanism: the writer mode is one record (`writers`); a migration is one compare-and-swap on it; every writable open is checked against it before the writer lock is taken

no_dual_authority.mechanism: one record, one CAS, every writable open checked before the lock
no_dual_authority.outside_the_protocol: a pre-record binary ignores the record (measured above)
no_dual_authority.window: none for a conforming writer: before the CAS the record says `from` and after it `to`; a writer opening in either window is admitted only for the recorded mode

old_binary.verdict: a pre-record binary is outside the protocol: it cannot be bound by the mode record, and its write is measured here rather than hidden. This is the documented residual risk; `min_reader` is the forward mechanism.

scope.checked: all six transition directions, live prepared transaction, crash at both sides of the CAS, a reader spanning the transition, and the v0.9.0 binary as an old reader and an old writer
scope.label: one host, one local POSIX namespace, process-fault proxies for the transition crash
scope.not_checked: multi-node coordination, clock skew, a distributed quiescence barrier, Go parity for the migration verb

transition_table.evidence: A, B: record created, single writes refused afterwards
C: a live prepared transaction blocks it; D: sharded writes/verify work afterwards
